title: Drawing interruptions reset inherited process state
summary: Test whether the 440 unanimous drawing interruptions define a semantic state reset: the first complete field after an interruption should reintroduce an owner or item cue, while an ordinary same-page gap should usually continue the prior state. This retains DIC001's distributed-reset result and the drawing-reset segment atlas, but does not infer picture ownership, words, or translation.

design.mechanism: A drawing interruption clears the active owner/item state and begins a new process segment; ordinary transcription spaces do not.
design.unit: eligible interruption and matched ordinary gap on the same folio/page, with adjacent cached fields
design.contrast: interruption versus equal-count, position- and folio-matched ordinary gap; include section and line-position nuisance controls
design.prediction: After interruptions, first fields have higher rates of explicit owner/item introduction and lower anaphoric continuation than after matched ordinary gaps, replicating across held folios and alternate readings.
design.scope: cached admitted transcription and DIC001/segment-atlas boundary inventory only; feasibility unknown for a clean owner/item coding panel
design.falsifier: No held-folio interaction after controls, or an effect explained by page position/line length alone, falsifies the reset-state mechanism; do not rescue it by changing boundary thresholds.
design.related: DIC001_drawing_interruption_target; drawing_reset_segment_atlas; DIC001 limitations explicitly prohibit picture-ownership or translation claims
